newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay launches Airbus test flight.
newsitem.headline: Cathay launches Airbus test flight.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said it began test flying one of its Airbus aircraft fitted with modified engines on Wednesday and planned to have its entire fleet of A330-300's back at work by mid-June.
The test-flight had been delayed since Tuesday afternoon due to technical problems arising from the aircraft having sat idle for the past 11 days, a company spokeswoman said.
"It's gone and it's actually now airborne. It went out this morning at 8.10 a.m. (0010 gmt)," the spokeswoman said, adding that the test-run would take about six hours.
"We meant to do the test flight yesterday but there were a couple of problems, but not associated with the engine parts."

Cathay and its 25.5 percent-owned Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) grounded their fleets of twin-engined A330-300 aircraft on May 24 after problems with Rolls-Royce Plc Trent 700 engines prompted a series of single-engine landings.
Cathay has 11 of the aircraft and Dragonair has four.
The problem stemmed from the lubrication system used in the Trent 700 gearbox and replacement parts arrived in Hong Kong on Monday.
"Assuming that all is successful and everything is fine...we hope to see the first aircraft in service possibly tomorrow and the others will get fitted in a continuing basis," she said.
She said the company planned to have its entire Airbus fleet back in operation by June 13. "But obviously, that's tentative."

The airline said in a statement had it had had to cancel 10 flights on Wednesday due to the suspension of its A330-300 services, but added it will be operating 91 percent of its flights andthat charters had been arranged with other airlines.
Chathay chairman Peter Sutch said last week that the grounding of the Airbus fleet would slice between HK$120 million and HK$150 million from its bottom line this year.
